source_artifacts.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)

capabilities.target: Directory profile and group memberships for a target user
User's MFA methods and issuance of a temporary pass
Chat message to the ticket requester containing the temporary pass

inputs.source: Support ticket submitted via the queue tool or emailed in, including tickets from contractors and vendors

instructions.note: Instructs the agent to send the temporary access pass 'to the person who opened the ticket' with no requirement that this person be verified as the account owner, so trust in the destination rests entirely on self-reported ticket metadata.

The prompt names analyst approval as the only named safety check ('every reset needs analyst approval'), but the approval gate covers only idp.reset_mfa, not the subsequent send_temp_pass step; no structural control is described for the send step itself.

autonomy.level is declared A2 (approval required on sensitive capabilities), but cap.send_temp_pass -- an S3 sink (egress of a restricted credential) -- has no approval_gate_ref. Per rubric section 3, this capability's effective autonomy is A3 (act then report), not A2 as the single reset-step gate implies.

controls.name: Service desk analyst approval gate on MFA reset
controls.decay_rationale: Enforced by a human analyst outside the model before idp.reset_mfa executes; the queue shows the raw target account, requester, and full ticket text (approval_review_mode: raw_action), so a more capable model cannot talk its way past it directly. It decays with approval volume (about 200 requests per analyst per shift, 'most are routine') rather than with model capability, and it does not validate that the self-reported requester is the verified account owner.

controls.name: Recipient confirmation bound to the verified account owner record
controls.decay_rationale: Would route the temporary pass to the account owner's registered contact in the directory system of record rather than to the ticket's self-reported requester field, so it would not decay with model capability or with social-engineering content in the ticket.

controls.name: Out-of-band identity verification of the ticket requester against the target account owner
controls.decay_rationale: Would require confirming the requester's identity through a channel outside the ticket itself (callback to a pre-registered number, manager attestation) before an analyst can approve, closing the gap that lets a consistent-looking but spoofed ticket pass raw-action review.

findings.title: Helpdesk social engineering MFA reset: temp pass sent to self-reported requester, not the verified account owner (confused deputy / TC4, consent-fatigue gate / TC9)

attack_path.note: Contractor/vendor email ticket requesting an MFA reset; the requester field is simply the email sender, unverified against the target account.
Agent looks up the target user and confirms the account exists.
Agent requests the reset; gated by ctl.analyst_approval, which reviews ticket content the attacker fully controls and cannot itself detect impersonation.
Agent sends the temporary pass to whoever opened the ticket -- the attacker-controlled requester identity, not the account owner -- with no separate approval.

findings.residual_rationale: The floor from crediting ctl.analyst_approval alone (structural, independent, raw_action review, step 2: -2 tiers from critical) would be moderate. Residual is rated high instead because the control's classification cannot express a design fact: the approver reviews only the ticket's own content (target, requester, ticket text), which is exactly the data an impersonating requester controls, and the gate does not cover cap.send_temp_pass at all, so once mfa_reset is approved the temp pass goes out automatically to whoever the ticket says opened it. No control verifies the requester is the account owner (ctl.identity_verification is missing), and no control binds the pass destination to the account owner's record (ctl.destination_binding is missing).

forecast.watch_signal: The analyst approval step for idp.reset_mfa is removed, bypassed, auto-approved, or narrowed (e.g., to spot-check sampling) under efficiency or volume pressure; or ticket/reset volume per analyst rises materially above the current ~200 per shift, the documented approval-fatigue trigger (SAFE-T1403) for this gate.

evidence.observation: Instructs the agent to look up the user, reset MFA, and 'send the temporary access pass to the person who opened the ticket' with no requirement to verify that person is the account owner.
States every reset needs analyst approval, but only the reset action is named; nothing requires approval or destination verification for the subsequent send step.

evidence.locator: approval queue (as shown to the analyst)
evidence.observation: The queue shows 'Requested by: <ticket requester>' alongside the target account and ticket text, but has no field or mechanism to confirm the requester is the target account's real owner.

'Contractors and vendors can email tickets in. The requester field is the email sender' and 'The temporary pass goes to whoever opened the ticket, not to the account owner' confirm the destination is bound to self-reported ticket metadata, not to a verified identity record.
'Two analysts cover the queue and approve about 400 requests per shift; most are routine' documents the approval volume behind the consent-fatigue risk for this gate.

recommendations.action: Bind the temporary pass destination to the account owner's registered contact method in the identity system of record; never send it to the ticket's self-reported requester field.

Require out-of-band verification of the requester's identity (callback to a pre-registered number, manager attestation, or equivalent) before the analyst can approve an MFA reset, especially for tickets from external or contractor email addresses.
Add an explicit approval or destination-confirmation gate on cap.send_temp_pass itself, independent of the mfa_reset approval.
Flag tickets where the requester's email domain is external (contractor/vendor) for mandatory secondary review, and monitor per-analyst approval rates for signs of fatigue-driven rubber-stamping.

rating.rationale: One present finding drives the rating. The path from an untrusted, email-submitted ticket through directory read, MFA reset (credential_access, S3), and automatic delivery of the temporary pass to the ticket's self-reported requester (egress of a restricted credential, S3) is inherently critical (U source to S3 sink). The only control on this path is a human analyst approval gate on the reset step with raw-action review, which earns a two-tier credit but does not verify requester identity or bind the pass destination to the account owner, so residual is held at high rather than the mechanical floor of moderate (see the finding's residual_rationale). Forecast returns to critical if the gate is removed, bypassed, or narrowed under autonomy increase or control removal, a plausible pressure point given the approval volume noted in the runtime notes (about 400 requests per shift across two analysts).

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration shown in prompt.md, the approval queue mockup, and the runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior of the deployed agent.

No tool manifest, MCP configuration, or IDP system configuration was provided; credential_scope and data_sensitivity for cap.mfa_reset, cap.user_read, and cap.send_temp_pass are inferred from the prompt and runtime notes rather than verified against a schema.

No information was provided on whether any identity-proofing or anomaly-detection process exists outside the described ticket and approval workflow; if one exists but was not disclosed in these artifacts, the rating would need revision.
